To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the rice bag has a lower attenuation factor than water does at TBI condition.
rice bags are 15% less attenuating than water at TBI conditions.
the TBI dose calculation with TMR based treatment plan system could underestimate the dose with rice bolus at the TBI treatment patient’s legs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the underdosage issue of TBI with rice bag bolus and provides a correction method to eliminate the overdose issue.
TMR based TBI treatment planning system and the effect of rice bag bolus placement at bilateral TBI treatment.
the effect of tissue equivalent bolus on TBI delivery.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the TMR based treatment plan system should be commissioned with rice bag phantons at TBI condition.
TBI patient treatment with rice bags should have the separation between the patient’s leg increased by 15% of the separation to compensate for the lower density of the rice bags.
TBI treatment planning system needs to be commissioned with TMR at TBI condition to correct the underestimation of rice bag bolus.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the rice bag is not a good bolus material for TBI treatment.
the rice bolus is not a good tissue equivalent material for TBI delivery.
the attenuation factor is a more accurate representation of tissue bolus than the electron density is for the TBI condition.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the rice bolus should be filled with enough thickness to cover the patient leg separation to avoid the underdosage issue.
the attenuation factor of the bolus material should be verified with the actual TBI conditions before using it in TBI treatment planning.
the TMR-based treatment planing systems are not accurate enough for TBI treatment planing.
